reference.source: Scriver's OMMBID / Nelson Textbook of Paediatrics
clinicalPearls: Defect in the final step of leucine catabolism and of ketogenesis, caused by biallelic HMGCL variants
Presents with acute episodes of hypoketotic hypoglycaemia and metabolic acidosis, often triggered by fasting or intercurrent illness
Hyperammonaemia and hepatomegaly frequently accompany crises, mimicking Reye syndrome
Because ketone body synthesis is blocked, hypoglycaemia occurs without appropriate ketosis (hypoketotic)
Urine organic acids show elevated 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutarate, 3-methylglutaconate, 3-methylglutarate and 3-hydroxyisovalerate
Diagnosis is supported by acylcarnitine profile (raised 3-methylglutaryl/3-hydroxyisovaleryl species) and confirmed by enzyme assay or HMGCL sequencing
Acute management is aggressive intravenous glucose to halt catabolism, with ammonia scavengers and correction of acidosis as needed
Long-term care combines avoidance of fasting, moderate protein/leucine restriction and carnitine supplementation
reference.pathophysiology: HMG-CoA lyase catalyses the final step of leucine degradation and the terminal reaction of hepatic ketogenesis, cleaving 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-CoA into acetoacetate and acetyl-CoA. Deficiency blocks both pathways, so during fasting or catabolic stress the liver cannot generate ketone bodies to provide alternative fuel, producing hypoketotic hypoglycaemia once glycogen stores are exhausted. Simultaneously, leucine-derived intermediates and organic acids accumulate, causing a high anion gap metabolic acidosis, and secondary inhibition of the urea cycle contributes to hyperammonaemia. The accumulating organic acids and energy failure injure the brain and liver, accounting for the encephalopathic, Reye-like crises. Inheritance is autosomal recessive.
additionalDifferentials: Fatty acid oxidation disorders (e.g. MCAD deficiency) with hypoketotic hypoglycaemia
Urea cycle disorders presenting with hyperammonaemia
Ketogenesis defects such as HMG-CoA synthase deficiency
additionalInvestigations: Urine organic acid analysis for the characteristic 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutarate and related acids
Plasma acylcarnitine profile by tandem mass spectrometry
Blood glucose, blood gas and ketone (beta-hydroxybutyrate) measurement during crises
HMGCL gene sequencing or enzyme assay in fibroblasts/leukocytes
Brain imaging if encephalopathic, to assess white-matter changes
redFlags: Hypoketotic hypoglycaemia with encephalopathy and coma
Significant hyperammonaemia during an acute crisis
Severe high anion gap metabolic acidosis
Reye-like hepatic dysfunction with rising transaminases
Rapid neurological deterioration during intercurrent illness or fasting
reference.prognosis: With early diagnosis, avoidance of fasting and prompt treatment of crises, many patients do well, but severe or delayed decompensations can cause permanent neurological injury or death, and outcome depends heavily on preventing metabolic crises.
pitfalls: Expecting ketosis to accompany hypoglycaemia and being falsely reassured by its absence
Misdiagnosing an acute crisis as Reye syndrome and missing the metabolic cause
Delaying intravenous glucose while awaiting confirmatory results
Overlooking hyperammonaemia as a treatable contributor to encephalopathy
Allowing prolonged fasting for procedures or illness without a metabolic emergency plan
references: Scriver's Online Metabolic and Molecular Bases of Inherited Disease (OMMBID)
Saudubray, Inborn Metabolic Diseases: Diagnosis and Treatment
